issues.feedback: The spec’s core execution model is not feasible as written: `tokio::runtime::Handle::current().block_on(...)` will panic when called from the daemon path running under `#[tokio::main]` (nested blocking on active runtime). This must be redesigned (async dispatch, `block_in_place` with constraints, or a fully synchronous backend execution path).

Config struct changes are specified, but CLI config surfaces are missing. `ralph config get/set/show` plumbing in `src/cli/config.rs` must add `workspace.daemon_refinement_enabled`, `workspace.daemon_refinement_backend`, `daemon.refinement_enabled`, and `daemon.refinement_backend`; otherwise users cannot manage the new settings through existing workflows.

Removing the synthetic fallback without defining failure policy for `fetch_issue_body` leaves behavior ambiguous when GitHub is unavailable, issue access fails, or issue is deleted. The spec should define deterministic behavior (retry policy, terminal transition, or explicit degraded fallback) to avoid indefinite pending-task churn.

Refinement is inserted into the synchronous dispatch path and may block up to backend timeout (default can be long). This can stall child collection and polling for extended periods. The spec should require a dedicated refinement timeout and non-blocking strategy to preserve daemon responsiveness.

The spec is internally inconsistent on where missing `raw_idea` is hydrated (`adopt_pending_tasks` vs `dispatch_task`). Pick one authoritative hydration point. Also clarify whether the `refined-prompt` comment is posted when refinement is disabled or when fallback-to-raw occurs, and what content/labeling is expected.

Current daemon validate fixtures commonly create pending tasks without `raw_idea`. With the proposed hydration behavior, those paths will call `gh issue view --json title,body`; existing mock gh scripts currently return empty output for `issue view`, which will break tests unless explicitly updated. This migration impact should be included in the test plan/acceptance criteria.
